title: Biggest Chain of Divisible Numbers
statement:
You get an array nums of distinct positive integers. Pick as many of them as possible so that for every pair you picked, the larger one is divisible by the smaller one.

Return one largest such group, in any order. If several groups have the largest size, any of them is accepted.

examples.why: 4 divides 8, 8 divides 16, and 4 divides 16. Starting from the smallest value, 3, only gives a group of one.
2 and 3 do not divide each other, so they cannot both be picked. [1, 3] is equally good.
No pair divides, so the best group has one number. Any single value is accepted.

constraints: All values in nums are different
hints: Sort the numbers. If a divides b and b divides c, does a divide c?
Divisibility is transitive, so after sorting a valid group is a chain where each element divides the next. You only need to check neighbours in the chain.
Let best[i] be the longest chain ending at nums[i]: 1 + the best best[j] over j < i with nums[i] % nums[j] == 0. Store the chosen j to rebuild the chain.

explain.intuition:
Checking every pair sounds expensive, but sorting removes most of the work. In sorted order, a valid group is a chain a₁ | a₂ | … | aₖ where each element divides the next. Divisibility is transitive, so if every neighbour pair divides, every pair does. The problem turns into "longest chain", like longest increasing subsequence with "divides" in place of "less than".

len[i] is the longest chain that ends with nums[i]. It extends the best chain ending at any earlier nums[j] that divides nums[i]. Remember that j as a parent pointer, then walk back from the best end to rebuild one answer.
steps: For each j < i with nums[i] % nums[j] == 0 and len[j] + 1 > len[i], set len[i] = len[j] + 1 and parent[i] = j.
Find the index with the largest len and follow parent back to collect the group.
pitfalls: Greedily building one chain from the smallest number. In the first example it starts at 3 and gets stuck at size 1.
Forgetting to sort first. Without sorting, the smaller-divides-larger check only goes one way and chains get missed.
Returning only the size. The task asks for the group itself, so keep parent pointers.

solutions.title: Try every subset
solutions.idea: Check all 2ⁿ subsets for the pairwise rule and keep the largest valid one.

solutions.title: Sort, then longest divisible chain
solutions.idea: After sorting, a valid group is a chain where each value divides the next. DP over the chain end with parent pointers.

followups: The values are at most 100 000 but there are 100 000 of them. Can you iterate over multiples instead of all earlier indexes?
Count how many different largest groups exist.
